chose: One clock drives the whole show: a pure timeline lays every scene out as its title typing in (0.6 s), its narration streaming line after line at 38 characters a second, the cubes turning (1.2 s) only once the copy has landed, each face's band label typing as it arrives, and a 4 s hold; an episode opens with the copy block turning about Y (1.4 s) and its cubes leave as the next episode's copy turns in. Every move is a keyframe track over the one cycle (about 105 s), each element's own keyframes, all with the same duration and named only on a wide screen with motion allowed, so nothing can drift or start out of step, however the page was opened. A line streams as a top-to-bottom wipe rather than a character at a time, because wrapped text can't be typed character by character in CSS alone; titles and labels, one line each, type a step a character. Each cube has four faces about X, its episode's scenes first. The whole show holds still under the pointer. On a phone and for a reader who prefers less motion, every episode lies flat: each scene's copy, then its two faces as cards in their own shapes. It moves C1112's ring of timed faces.
options: one build-time timeline of keyframe tracks over one cycle
